Bug_Title: Loops with at most one iteration should be refactored
Bug_Details:
A loop with at most one iteration is equivalent to an if statement. This can confuse developers and make the code less readable since
loops are not meant to replace if statements.
If the intention was to conditionally execute the block only once, an if statement should be used instead. Otherwise, the loop should
be fixed so the loop block can be executed multiple times.
A loop statement with at most one iteration can happen when a statement that unconditionally transfers control, such as a jump or throw statement,
is misplaced inside the loop block.
This rule arises when the following statements are misplaced:
break return throw
break
return
throw
Bug_Explanation: The for-loop in the showBug method is designed to iterate over an array, but due to the 'break' statement inside the loop, it only allows at most one iteration. This loop should be refactored to use an 'if' statement instead to improve readability as it effectively performs a check-and-execute once.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases use arrays of varying lengths, including an empty array, to trigger the bug in the showBug method, which uses a loop that effectively only ever executes once due to an unconditional break. These assertions expose the incorrect behavior, expecting the loop to iterate multiple times but failing because it only iterates once.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that all tests passed successfully without any errors or failures, suggesting that the bug was not triggered during the test execution.
